3.​ Add after paragraph 15 and renumber (Bath) 
 
The ruling class's desperate hope that AI will provide a miracle to boost stagnating 
productivity is a massive, speculative bubble. Nearly 40 percent of US GDP growth is 
currently attributed to AI, however the $860bn invested in 2025 only returned $35bn in 
revenue. This is clearly an orgy of speculation being fueled by fictitious capital and a 
dangerous expansion of the shadow banking sector. The global economy is 
precariously vulnerable to a devastating crash, which will lead to vicious attacks on 
the world working class. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject in favour of amendment 7 
  
4.​ Add after paragraph 23 and renumber (Preston Ribble) 
 
British imperialism’s short-sightedness is clear in the North of Ireland, where decades 
of deindustrialisation, as well as the economic dislocation caused by Brexit, have 
turned a formerly valuable, industrialised colonial possession into an economic and 
political burden for the British state. For example, the North of Ireland now has the 
UK’s highest rate of economic inactivity and consistently ranks bottom in the UK for 
disposable income. The deficiencies of the 1998 Good Friday Agreement – once 
hailed by Westminster as the end of sectarian division and instability – are now being 
revealed in full. After presiding over crisis and decline, the Unionist establishment 
and its main parties are being discredited, with the more hardcore TUV now picking 
up a share of the loyalist vote. Meanwhile, the left-nationalist Sinn Féin is topping the 
polls. The social crisis in Ireland, alongside simmering sectarian tensions and 
political paralysis in Stormont, could see the North have a further destabilising effect 
on the Union as a whole. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject 
 
5.​ Add after paragraph 25 and renumber (Cambridge UoC) 
 
Much of today’s economy is increasingly tied to expectations about the future value 
of AI. There is, for example, massive investment from the “Magnificent Seven” tech 
companies in AI technology. For many investors, AI is seen as a potential lifeline for 
the capitalist system, promising new growth and productivity. However, speculation 
around AI is significantly outpacing its realistically achievable value, giving rise to an 
AI bubble. 
 
With global debt estimated at roughly 350% of GDP, the world economy is in a 
particularly weak position to absorb a major shock. If such a bubble were to burst, 
capitalism would fall into an even more pronounced slump and, as in past crises, the 
burden would fall on the shoulders of the working class. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject in favour of amendment 7
